## Approved policies

| ID | User decision and implementation interpretation | Required verification cases |
|---|---|---|
| HQ-01 / GOV-015 | If pre-existing uncommitted changes exist when work starts, ask the user to either authorize a commit or suspend the task for manual intervention. In headless mode without a standing choice, stop safely. Prior authorization is valid only within its stated scope; generic approval of a workflow is not blanket authorization. An explicit user request to rewrite `main` is valid unless another applicable policy prohibits it. | Dirty and clean working trees; staged, unstaged and untracked content; unrelated changes; unattended/headless run; explicit and implicit permission for reset, force-push and `main` rewrites. Never test destructive operations in the actual research repository. |
| HQ-02 / RUN-021 | Cache invalidation/update must preserve coherence with a successfully committed authoritative data mutation. The chosen strategy must account for transaction isolation, concurrency, non-atomicity across the database and Redis, crashes and retries. Pre-commit invalidation is not categorically forbidden if its correctness is demonstrated. | Successful commit; rollback; crash between commit and invalidation; concurrent reader/refill; transaction-isolation variations; explicitly documented tolerance for staleness. |
| HQ-03 / DEP-003 | An explicit, scoped user request can permit a floating dependency version; hooks/checkers must support the controlled exception while retaining the default prohibition. | Unapproved version rejected; approved version accepted; approval scope; exact-version verification; no global disabling of protections. |
| HQ-04 / GOV-017 | Headless execution may **implement** an expressly pre-approved Reserved change; it must not autonomously **make** a new Reserved decision. | Pre-approved action permitted; vague broad task is insufficient; new Reserved choice pauses; decision recorded. |
| HQ-05 / DEP-025 | A generic confirmation prompt (`ask`) or command-comment marker does not override the requirement to resolve incompatible peer dependencies. Do not introduce an automatic bypass path. A special research-specific policy exception requires a separate explicit decision. | `--force`, `--legacy-peer-deps`, magic markers, direct shell commands, workflows; no bypass through approval UI; positive compatibility-resolution cases. |
| HQ-06 / PI-012 | Apply the refined methodology: distinguish actual semantics, modality/normative strength and the source's authority. Logically equivalent `only when` and `do not unless` in the same normative context must be assessed equivalently; a technical example is not automatically MUST_NOT because it contains a negation. Review all 230 additional candidates without assuming they are mistakes. | Original 79 and 230 additional leads; independent counterexample checks; blind comparison where feasible; sensitivity analysis of the metrics. |

## Mandatory loop for ONE logical rule correction

1. **Baseline.** Identify all affected inventory policies, authoritative owner files, dependencies, hooks/checkers, test suites, before-hashes, and previously repaired cases.
2. **Atomic correction.** Fix exactly ONE semantic rule, together with all of its directly linked implementation surfaces where necessary. Do not make the next logically separate correction yet.
3. **Local semantic check.** Validate the canonical contract and every related policy, applicability condition, permitted exception, priority, ownership, routing/loading and scope.
4. **Complete affected-architecture check.** Verify structure, internal references, authoritative ownership and mapping against all 194 V2-derived policies plus `GOV-017/018` in every affected candidate architecture; disclose any discrepancy.
5. **Positive/negative tests.** Add tests of allowed and forbidden behavior, exceptions, failure and concurrency scenarios where relevant; exercise hooks/checkers in disposable fixtures.
6. **Cumulative regression.** Recheck **ALL previous corrections**, even across different files; re-evaluate six-candidate parity for the affected obligations.
7. **Gate.** If ANY applicable check fails, repair/rollback the current atomic change and repeat steps 3–6. Do not start the next rule without a successful gate.
8. **Independent final sweep after ALL corrections.** Re-verify 196 × 6 obligations, source and classification provenance (6,402 originals plus approved new proposals), all previously repaired conditions, interacting rules, 230 PI-012 leads, hooks/checkers, structural integrity, cross-change regressions and a separate final audit. Save the complete results.

**Historical scope note:** At the time this register was originally created, no frozen `inputs/*/output/template/` trees had been edited and no live post-repair runtime tests had been run. For the current v2 task, this register is an approval/verification reference, NOT a statement about today's v1 repaired state. Revalidate all claims against the v1 handoff and current v2 source files.
